fields.label: Heading
fields.value: Your Visits & Our Practice

fields.label: Intro paragraph
fields.value: First appointments, nerves, kids, parking and who you’ll see.

fields.label: Text
fields.value: I'm anxious about the dentist, can you help?

fields.label: Paragraph
fields.value: If you feel anxious, tell us. We'll take things at your pace, explain each step, and use gentle techniques and comfort options such as in-chair entertainment to help you relax.

fields.label: Text
fields.value: About Us

fields.label: Text
fields.value: What kind of dentistry do you do?

fields.label: Paragraph
fields.value: General and preventative care, cosmetic work, restorative dentistry including crowns and dentures, dental implants, orthodontics and children’s dentistry - plus emergency appointments. If something falls outside what we do well, we’ll refer you rather than attempt it.

fields.label: Text
fields.value: Do you see children?

fields.label: Paragraph
fields.value: Yes, and we like to. Zoe, our oral health therapist, looks after patients under 18, and eligible children can be bulk billed through the Child Dental Benefits Schedule.

fields.label: Text
fields.value: Are you taking new patients?

fields.label: Paragraph
fields.value: Yes. New patients can book online any time, and the first visit is no-gap with a participating health fund rebating $199 or more, or a flat $199 without cover. A $50 booking deposit applies and comes off the visit.

fields.label: Text
fields.value: New Patients

fields.label: Text
fields.value: How long is the first appointment?

fields.label: Paragraph
fields.value: Allow about an hour. That gives us time to listen properly, examine thoroughly, take any X-rays, do your scale and clean, and talk through the plan without rushing you.

fields.label: Text
fields.value: What should I bring?

fields.label: Paragraph
fields.value: Your health fund card if you have one, your Medicare card (for CDBS-eligible children), a list of current medications, and your completed medical history form. If you have recent X-rays from another practice, bring those too - it may save repeating them.

fields.label: Text
fields.value: I’m embarrassed about my teeth. Will that be a problem?

fields.label: Paragraph
fields.value: Not here. There is nothing we haven’t seen, and no judgement waiting for you. Most people who’ve stayed away for years tell us the hardest part was the phone call.

fields.label: Text
fields.value: What does the first visit cost?

fields.label: Paragraph
fields.value: For new patients it’s no-gap where your health fund rebates $199 or more, or a flat $199 without cover - including exam, treatment plan, X-rays, scale and clean, and fluoride. A $50 booking deposit applies and comes off the visit. Full terms on our offers page.

fields.label: Text
fields.value: Contact & Finding Us

fields.label: Text
fields.value: Do I need an appointment?

fields.label: Paragraph
fields.value: Not necessarily - walk-ins are welcome and we keep time aside for emergencies. Booking ahead means less waiting, and you can do it online at any hour.

fields.label: Text
fields.value: How quickly will you reply to an enquiry?

fields.label: Paragraph
fields.value: We aim to respond within one business day. If it’s urgent or clinical, please ring instead of using the form.

fields.label: Text
fields.value: Where exactly are you?

fields.label: Paragraph
fields.value: {{site:street}}, East Maitland - beside Australia Post, with the Lila & Allan hair salon next door. There’s a bus stop directly opposite and parking at the rear.

fields.label: Text
fields.value: Our Clinic

fields.label: Text
fields.value: Is there parking?

fields.label: Paragraph
fields.value: Yes - on-street parking on Lawes Street, council parking near Your Discount Chemist, and parking at the rear of the practice.

fields.label: Text
fields.value: Is the practice wheelchair accessible?

fields.label: Paragraph
fields.value: Yes. There’s an entrance ramp, easy access throughout, and an accessible toilet. The entry is pram-friendly too.

fields.label: Text
fields.value: Can I bring my children with me?

fields.label: Paragraph
fields.value: Of course. There’s a play area in the waiting room, and our team are used to keeping an eye on little ones while a parent is in the chair.

fields.label: Text
fields.value: Our Team

fields.label: Text
fields.value: Can I ask to see a particular person?

fields.label: Paragraph
fields.value: Yes - just say so when you book. If they’re away or fully booked we’ll tell you honestly rather than quietly putting you with someone else.

fields.label: Text
fields.value: Are your dentists specialists?

fields.label: Paragraph
fields.value: Dr Nish and Dr Nav are general dentists, not registered specialists. Dr Nav holds a Fellowship of the Royal Australasian College of Dental Surgeons, a postgraduate qualification in managing complex cases. Where a case needs a registered specialist, we refer.

fields.label: Text
fields.value: Who will see my children?

fields.label: Paragraph
fields.value: Usually Zoe, our oral health therapist, who treats patients under 18 for check-ups, cleans, fillings, sealants and baby-tooth extractions. If something needs a dentist, one is a few steps away.

fields.label: Text
fields.value: Our Technology

fields.label: Text
fields.value: Do I still need X-rays if you have a camera?

fields.label: Paragraph
fields.value: Yes - they show different things. The intraoral camera photographs surfaces you can see; X-rays show what’s between and beneath teeth, and inside bone. We take the minimum needed to diagnose properly.

fields.label: Text
fields.value: How do I know instruments are clean?

fields.label: Paragraph
fields.value: Instruments are cleaned and sterilised in a dedicated room, then vacuum-packed and kept sealed until opened in front of you. Our protocols meet or exceed ADA and Australian government standards and are checked daily.

fields.label: Text
fields.value: Choosing Treatment

fields.label: Text
fields.value: Where do I start if I don’t know what’s wrong?

fields.label: Paragraph
fields.value: With a check-up. We examine, take any X-rays we need, show you what we find on screen and give you options with prices. You leave knowing where you stand, whether or not you book anything further.

fields.label: Text
fields.value: Do you offer payment plans on larger treatment?

fields.label: Paragraph
fields.value: Yes - interest-free plans through Humm and DentiCare, and for some essential treatment the ATO’s Compassionate Release of Super may apply. Lending criteria, fees and terms and conditions apply.

fields.label: Text
fields.value: Conditions & Symptoms

fields.label: Text
fields.value: What if my symptom isn’t listed?

fields.label: Paragraph
fields.value: Call us on {{site:phone}} and describe it - plain words are fine. A short conversation is usually enough for us to know how soon you should be seen and by whom.

fields.label: Text
fields.value: Do I need a referral?

fields.label: Paragraph
fields.value: No. You can book directly with us for anything on this page, online or by phone. If something ever needs a specialist, we’ll refer you and explain why.

fields.label: Text
fields.value: How do I know if it’s an emergency?

fields.label: Paragraph
fields.value: Severe or ongoing pain, a knocked-out or broken tooth, uncontrolled bleeding or facial swelling all count - go to our emergency page or just call. When in doubt, ring; we’d rather tell you it can wait than have you wait when it can’t.

fields.label: Text
fields.value: What does the new-patient offer include?

fields.label: Paragraph
fields.value: Your first visit covers a comprehensive examination, personalised treatment plan, X-rays, a scale and clean, and a fluoride treatment. We'll waive the gap where your fund rebates at least $199, or it's a flat $199 without cover. For new patients only; a $50 booking deposit applies and comes off the cost of your visit.

fields.label: Text
fields.value: Do I pay on the day?

fields.label: Paragraph
fields.value: Yes - payment is due on the day of treatment. With HICAPS we claim from your health fund on the spot, so you only pay any gap. For larger treatment plans, Humm and DentiCare let you spread the cost interest-free (lending criteria, fees and T&Cs apply).

fields.label: Text
fields.value: Which health funds do you take?

fields.label: Paragraph
fields.value: All of them. We have HICAPS for on-the-spot claiming with funds including HCF, Bupa, Medibank, nib, CBHS, Teachers Health, Defence Health, Australian Unity and GMHBA. Your rebate depends on your policy - bring your card and we’ll check it before treatment.

fields.label: Text
fields.value: Is my child covered by CDBS?

fields.label: Paragraph
fields.value: Children aged 0–17 who meet Services Australia’s criteria get up to $1,158 of basic dental services over two consecutive calendar years, and we bulk bill it. Check eligibility on the Services Australia website or ask reception to help you check.

fields.label: Text
fields.value: Can I really use my super for dental work?

fields.label: Paragraph
fields.value: For essential treatment, the ATO’s Compassionate Release of Super can apply - implants, dentures, surgery, orthodontics, root canal and crowns among them. SuperCare facilitates applications for our patients and charges nothing unless approved. It’s a formal ATO process, so allow time.

fields.label: Text
fields.value: Can I combine offers?

fields.label: Paragraph
fields.value: One offer per visit - the seniors discount can’t stack on the new-patient offer, and CDBS is a Medicare benefit rather than a practice offer. If two could apply, we’ll use whichever leaves you better off.

fields.label: Text
fields.value: Why is there a $50 deposit on the new-patient offer?

fields.label: Paragraph
fields.value: It holds your appointment and comes straight off the cost of your visit - you don’t pay it twice. If you need to move your appointment, give us a ring and we’ll carry it over.

fields.label: Text
fields.value: Is whitening suitable for everyone?

fields.label: Paragraph
fields.value: No - and we’ll tell you honestly. Whitening works on natural tooth surfaces and not on crowns, veneers or fillings, and some causes of discolouration need a different approach. That’s why every whitening offer starts with a suitability assessment. Results vary from person to person.

fields.label: Small label above the heading
fields.value: General & Preventative Dentistry

fields.label: Heading
fields.value: General & Preventative Dentistry

fields.label: Intro paragraph
fields.value: Check-ups, cleans, gum care, extractions, wisdom teeth and kids’ dentistry.

fields.label: Text
fields.value: Preventative Care

fields.label: Text
fields.value: Does a clean damage enamel?

fields.label: Paragraph
fields.value: No. Ultrasonic scalers and polishing remove calculus and stain from the tooth surface - they don’t remove healthy enamel. Sensitivity for a day or two afterwards is common, especially where gums have receded, and settles.

fields.label: Text
fields.value: Is CDBS really free?

fields.label: Paragraph
fields.value: For covered basic services, yes - we bulk bill it, so eligible children pay nothing out of pocket up to the cap. It doesn’t cover orthodontics or cosmetic work. Eligibility is set by Services Australia and we can help you check it.

fields.label: Text
fields.value: General Dentistry

fields.label: Text
fields.value: Will I need X-rays every time?

fields.label: Paragraph
fields.value: No. We take them when there’s a clinical reason, checking between teeth, under existing fillings, or around roots, not as a routine at every visit. Digital sensors keep the dose low.

fields.label: Text
fields.value: Can I have several things done in one appointment?

fields.label: Paragraph
fields.value: Often, yes, and it saves you trips. It depends on how long you can comfortably sit, whether the areas need separate anaesthetic, and what your day looks like afterwards. We’ll plan it with you.

fields.label: Text
fields.value: What if I’ve avoided the dentist for years?

fields.label: Paragraph
fields.value: You’ll be in good company, and there’s no lecture. We’ll examine, tell you honestly where things stand, and build a plan in a sensible order - usually comfort and infection first, appearance later.

fields.label: Text
fields.value: Check-ups & Examinations

fields.label: Text
fields.value: How long does a check-up take?

fields.label: Paragraph
fields.value: Allow about 30 to 40 minutes for an examination, or around an hour if you’re a new patient having a clean as well. We’d rather take the time than rush and miss something.

fields.label: Text
fields.value: How often should I come?

fields.label: Paragraph
fields.value: Six months suits most people. Low-risk patients with stable gums may stretch to twelve; anyone with gum disease, high decay risk or a dry mouth benefits from three or four monthly. We’ll recommend an interval and explain why.

fields.label: Text
fields.value: Do you check for mouth cancer?

fields.label: Paragraph
fields.value: Yes, as part of every examination - tongue, floor of mouth, cheeks, palate and throat. It takes under a minute and it is one of the more important minutes of the appointment.

fields.label: Text
fields.value: I’m nervous. Can I just have a look and a chat first?

fields.label: Paragraph
fields.value: Absolutely. Book an examination, tell us when you arrive, and we’ll go at your pace - including stopping at just a look and a conversation if that’s where you want to leave it that day.

fields.label: Text
fields.value: Scale, Clean & Oral Hygiene

fields.label: Text
fields.value: Does a scale and clean hurt?

fields.label: Paragraph
fields.value: For most people it’s a strange sensation rather than a painful one - vibration, water and a bit of scraping. If your gums are inflamed or roots are exposed it can be tender, and we can numb the area. Tell us and we’ll adjust.

fields.label: Text
fields.value: Will it whiten my teeth?

fields.label: Paragraph
fields.value: It removes surface staining from coffee, tea, wine and smoking, so teeth usually look brighter and cleaner. It doesn’t change the underlying colour of the tooth - that’s what whitening does.

fields.label: Text
fields.value: How often should I have one?

fields.label: Paragraph
fields.value: Six months suits most people. If you build tartar quickly, smoke, or have a history of gum disease, three or four monthly is often better for a while. We’ll recommend an interval based on what we actually see.

fields.label: Text
fields.value: Is floss really necessary?

fields.label: Paragraph
fields.value: Something between the teeth is necessary - brushing only reaches about 60% of the surfaces. Whether that’s floss, interdental brushes or a water flosser depends on the size of your gaps. Zoe will work out which suits your mouth.

fields.label: Text
fields.value: Gum (Periodontal) Treatment

fields.label: Text
fields.value: Is gum disease reversible?

fields.label: Paragraph
fields.value: Gingivitis is - the early stage, where gums bleed but no bone has been lost, resolves fully with treatment and good daily cleaning. Periodontitis, where bone has gone, can be stabilised and controlled but not reversed. That difference is exactly why we push early treatment.

fields.label: Text
fields.value: Does deep cleaning hurt?

fields.label: Paragraph
fields.value: It’s done under local anaesthetic, so the appointment itself shouldn’t hurt. Afterwards expect tenderness and cold sensitivity for a few days as the gums heal and tighten.

fields.label: Text
fields.value: Why do I need to come every three months now?

fields.label: Paragraph
fields.value: Bacteria repopulate deep pockets in roughly 12 weeks. Three-monthly maintenance interrupts that cycle. It’s the difference between keeping your teeth and slowly losing them, and it’s the part people most often let slide.

fields.label: Text
fields.value: Can gum disease affect my general health?

fields.label: Paragraph
fields.value: There are well-documented associations between periodontal disease and diabetes, cardiovascular disease and adverse pregnancy outcomes. The relationships are complex and still being studied, but treating gum inflammation is sensible for reasons beyond your mouth.

fields.label: Text
fields.value: Children's Dentistry

fields.label: Text
fields.value: When should my child first see a dentist?

fields.label: Paragraph
fields.value: By their first birthday or when the first tooth appears. That first visit is mostly about familiarity, a look, a count, a sticker, and it makes every visit after it easier.

fields.label: Text
fields.value: Do baby teeth really need filling if they’ll fall out anyway?

fields.label: Paragraph
fields.value: Often yes. A decaying baby tooth can become painful, infect the adult tooth developing beneath it, and if it’s lost too early the neighbouring teeth drift into the space. That said, we do weigh how close the tooth is to falling out naturally.

fields.label: Text
fields.value: What if my child won’t open their mouth?

fields.label: Paragraph
fields.value: Then we don’t force it. We’ll try again, keep the visit short and positive, and build up over a few appointments. Almost every child gets there - the ones who don’t are usually the ones who were pushed too hard, too early.

fields.label: Text
fields.value: Should my seven-year-old see an orthodontist?

fields.label: Paragraph
fields.value: An assessment around seven is worthwhile, not because treatment usually starts then, but because a growing jaw gives options that disappear later. We’ll tell you honestly if there’s nothing to do yet.

fields.label: Text
fields.value: Mouthguards & Splints

fields.label: Text
fields.value: Why not just buy one from the chemist?

fields.label: Paragraph
fields.value: A boil-and-bite guard is loose by design, so it moves, it’s bulky to breathe and talk through, and it absorbs less impact. As a night splint the problem is worse - an ill-fitting one can shift your bite or aggravate the jaw joint. A custom appliance is made to your teeth and adjusted in your mouth.

fields.label: Text
fields.value: How long does a mouthguard last?

fields.label: Paragraph
fields.value: An adult sports guard typically lasts one to three seasons depending on how hard it’s used. Children need replacing far more often as their teeth change - often every season. Splints usually last several years but wear faster in heavy grinders.

fields.label: Text
fields.value: Will a splint stop me grinding?

fields.label: Paragraph
fields.value: No, and anyone promising that is overselling. It protects your teeth from the forces you generate, so the wear happens to the acrylic instead of your enamel. Reducing stress, caffeine and alcohol, and sorting out sleep, is what reduces the grinding itself.

fields.label: Text
fields.value: Can my child wear a mouthguard with braces?

fields.label: Paragraph
fields.value: Yes, and they absolutely should - a knock with fixed braces can do serious soft tissue damage. The guard is made to accommodate the brackets and will need remaking as teeth move.

fields.label: Text
fields.value: Laser Dentistry

fields.label: Text
fields.value: Does laser gum treatment hurt?

fields.label: Paragraph
fields.value: Usually less than the conventional alternative. Many procedures are done with just topical or local anaesthetic, and afterwards is typically mild soreness rather than real pain. If you’re anxious, say so - we’ll numb generously.

fields.label: Text
fields.value: How long until it looks right?

fields.label: Paragraph
fields.value: You’ll see the change immediately, but gums keep settling for two to four weeks and the final contour appears over that time. For cosmetic cases we take photographs to compare properly.

fields.label: Text
fields.value: Will the gum grow back?

fields.label: Paragraph
fields.value: Healthy reshaped gum generally stays where it’s put. Regrowth happens most often where the underlying cause is still active - certain medications, ongoing inflammation, or plaque around the area.

fields.label: Text
fields.value: Is it suitable for children?

fields.label: Paragraph
fields.value: Frenectomy in children is one of the more common uses, and the laser makes it quicker and less distressing than the traditional approach. We assess each child individually.

fields.label: Text
fields.value: Tooth Extraction

fields.label: Text
fields.value: Will it hurt?

fields.label: Paragraph
fields.value: The extraction itself shouldn’t - local anaesthetic handles that, and we test the area before starting. You’ll feel firm pressure, which is normal. Afterwards expect soreness for a few days, usually manageable with over-the-counter pain relief.

fields.label: Text
fields.value: How long is the recovery?

fields.label: Paragraph
fields.value: Most of the discomfort settles within three to five days. The gum surface closes over in a couple of weeks, while the bone underneath continues remodelling for several months.

fields.label: Text
fields.value: Can I go back to work afterwards?

fields.label: Paragraph
fields.value: After a simple extraction, most people do. After a surgical one, take the rest of the day. Avoid heavy lifting and strenuous exercise for 24 to 48 hours either way.

fields.label: Text
fields.value: What should replace the tooth?

fields.label: Paragraph
fields.value: Depends on which tooth and what surrounds it - an implant, a bridge, a partial denture, or occasionally nothing. It’s worth deciding before the extraction, since some options are easier to plan while the tooth is still there.

fields.label: Text
fields.value: Wisdom Teeth Removal

fields.label: Text
fields.value: Do all wisdom teeth need to come out?

fields.label: Paragraph
fields.value: No, and the idea that they do is outdated. If they’ve come through straight, you can clean them, and they’re causing no problems, leave them. We remove them when there’s a reason.

fields.label: Text
fields.value: Will I be asleep?

fields.label: Paragraph
fields.value: Most cases are done here under local anaesthetic, awake but numb. For complex impactions or very anxious patients, referral for sedation or general anaesthetic is an option we’ll discuss.

fields.label: Text
fields.value: How much time off should I plan?

fields.label: Paragraph
fields.value: Two to three days for most people, ideally over a weekend. Avoid strenuous exercise for about a week, since raising your blood pressure can restart bleeding.

fields.label: Text
fields.value: What is dry socket and how do I avoid it?

fields.label: Paragraph
fields.value: It’s when the blood clot is lost from the socket, leaving bone exposed - intensely painful, usually starting three to five days after. Avoid it by not smoking, not using straws, and not rinsing vigorously for the first 24 hours. If it happens, come in; we can dress the socket and it settles quickly.

fields.label: Text
fields.value: Is the 3D scan necessary?

fields.label: Paragraph
fields.value: Not for every case. For lower wisdom teeth where a standard X-ray suggests the roots are near the nerve, it changes how we plan and sometimes whether we operate at all. That’s worth the scan.

fields.label: Heading
fields.value: Cosmetic Dentistry

fields.label: Intro paragraph
fields.value: Whitening, veneers and smile makeovers.

fields.label: Text
fields.value: Cosmetic Dentistry

fields.label: Text
fields.value: Will whitening work on my teeth?

fields.label: Paragraph
fields.value: It works on natural tooth surfaces and not on crowns, veneers or fillings, which stay the colour they were made. Some causes of discolouration respond much better than others, which is why every whitening starts with an assessment. Results vary from person to person.

fields.label: Text
fields.value: How long does cosmetic work last?

fields.label: Paragraph
fields.value: With good care, porcelain veneers commonly last ten years or more and composite bonding rather less. Whitening fades gradually and is usually topped up. Grinding, biting nails or opening things with your teeth shortens all of it.

fields.label: Text
fields.value: Can I see what it will look like first?

fields.label: Paragraph
fields.value: For larger cases, yes - we plan digitally from photographs and can trial the proposed shape in your mouth before committing to porcelain. It’s the surest way to know the result suits your face, not just your teeth.

fields.label: Text
fields.value: Is any of it painful?

fields.label: Paragraph
fields.value: Whitening can cause temporary sensitivity for a day or so. Veneer preparation is done under local anaesthetic, and afterwards is usually mild. We’ll talk through comfort options if you’re anxious.

fields.label: Text
fields.value: Teeth Whitening

fields.label: Text
fields.value: How white will my teeth actually go?

fields.label: Paragraph
fields.value: Most people lift several shades, but the honest answer is that it depends on your starting colour and the cause of the discolouration. Age-related yellowing responds well. Grey tones and tetracycline staining respond poorly. We’ll give you a realistic expectation at the assessment, and results vary from person to person.

fields.label: Text
fields.value: In-chair or take-home - which is better?

fields.label: Paragraph
fields.value: In-chair is faster and supervised throughout, so it suits an event or anyone impatient. Take-home trays give a more gradual result that’s often gentler on sensitivity, and you keep the trays for cheap top-ups later. Many people do in-chair first and maintain with trays.

fields.label: Text
fields.value: Does whitening damage enamel?

fields.label: Paragraph
fields.value: Professionally supervised whitening at appropriate concentrations doesn’t damage enamel. Sensitivity during treatment is common and temporary. The real risks come from unsupervised products, ill-fitting trays and overuse.

fields.label: Text
fields.value: How long will it last?

fields.label: Paragraph
fields.value: Typically one to three years, though it varies enormously with diet and smoking. Occasional top-ups with your take-home trays keep it going with much less effort than starting from scratch.

fields.label: Text
fields.value: Can I whiten if I have fillings on my front teeth?

fields.label: Paragraph
fields.value: You can, but they won’t change colour, so they may need replacing afterwards to match your new shade. That cost should be part of your decision, and we’ll price it up front.

fields.label: Text
fields.value: Veneers & Laminates

fields.label: Text
fields.value: How many veneers will I need?

fields.label: Paragraph
fields.value: It depends on how wide your smile shows. Some people need two, most who want a noticeable change have six to eight across the front, and full upper and lower cases exist. We plan from photographs of your actual smile rather than a formula.

fields.label: Text
fields.value: Do veneers ruin your teeth?

fields.label: Paragraph
fields.value: Traditional veneers permanently remove some enamel, and that tooth will always need covering afterwards. It isn’t damage exactly, but it is a lifelong commitment and you deserve to hear it plainly before you agree. Minimal-prep veneers and composite bonding are more conservative alternatives.

fields.label: Text
fields.value: Will they look fake?

fields.label: Paragraph
fields.value: Only if they’re designed to. Good veneers vary slightly in shape and translucency, follow the curve of your lip and match your face and age. We’ll talk you out of uniform, blinding white if you ask for it.

fields.label: Text
fields.value: What happens if one chips?

fields.label: Paragraph
fields.value: Small chips can sometimes be polished or repaired with composite. Larger damage usually means remaking that veneer. Bring it in rather than living with it - a rough edge irritates the tongue and can trap plaque.

fields.label: Text
fields.value: Can I have veneers if I grind my teeth?

fields.label: Paragraph
fields.value: Yes, but a night splint becomes mandatory rather than advisable. Grinding is the single biggest cause of veneer failure. If you won’t wear a splint, we’d rather discuss alternatives.

fields.label: Text
fields.value: Smile Makeover

fields.label: Text
fields.value: How long does a smile makeover take?

fields.label: Paragraph
fields.value: From a few weeks for whitening and bonding, to eighteen months or more if orthodontics is part of the plan. We’ll give you a realistic timeline at the planning stage, including the waiting periods between phases.

fields.label: Text
fields.value: Can I see what it will look like before committing?

fields.label: Paragraph
fields.value: Yes, and you should. We design digitally from photographs and can trial the proposed shape in your mouth. It’s the surest way to avoid disappointment, and it’s reversible.

fields.label: Text
fields.value: Will it look natural?

fields.label: Paragraph
fields.value: That’s the aim, and it’s mostly about restraint - appropriate proportions, slight variation between teeth, a shade that suits your age and complexion. If you ask for something we think will look artificial, we’ll tell you.

fields.label: Text
fields.value: Do I have to do it all at once?

fields.label: Paragraph
fields.value: No. Many people stage it over a couple of years, which spreads the cost and lets health fund limits reset. We’ll sequence it so each phase is a sensible stopping point.

fields.label: Small label above the heading
fields.value: Restorative Dentistry & Implants

fields.label: Heading
fields.value: Restorative Dentistry & Implants

fields.label: Intro paragraph
fields.value: Fillings, crowns, bridges, dentures, implants and root canal treatment.

fields.label: Text
fields.value: White Fillings

fields.label: Text
fields.value: How long will a white filling last?

fields.label: Paragraph
fields.value: Typically five to ten years, sometimes considerably longer for small ones. Lifespan depends on size, position, whether you grind, and how well the area is kept clean. No filling is permanent.

fields.label: Text
fields.value: Should I replace my amalgam fillings?

fields.label: Paragraph
fields.value: Not just because they’re amalgam. If one is sound, replacing it removes healthy tooth for no clinical gain. If it’s cracked, leaking, decayed underneath, or you dislike the appearance and understand the trade-off, that’s a fair reason.

fields.label: Text
fields.value: Why is my tooth sensitive after a filling?

fields.label: Paragraph
fields.value: The tooth has been irritated by the procedure, and deeper cavities sit closer to the nerve. Sensitivity to cold for a week or two is normal. If it’s getting worse rather than better, or hurts when you bite, ring us - it may simply be a high spot.

fields.label: Text
fields.value: Can you match the colour exactly?

fields.label: Paragraph
fields.value: We shade-match to your surrounding teeth and it’s usually indistinguishable. Two things to know: the match is to your teeth as they are now, so later whitening will leave the filling behind; and composite picks up stain over years while enamel doesn’t, so a perfect match can drift.

fields.label: Text
fields.value: Root Canal Treatment

fields.label: Text
fields.value: Is root canal treatment as bad as people say?

fields.label: Paragraph
fields.value: The reputation comes from decades ago. With modern anaesthetic and instruments, most people find the appointment much like having a large filling - long, but not painful. The severe pain people associate with it is usually the infection beforehand, which the treatment relieves.

fields.label: Text
fields.value: How many appointments will it take?

fields.label: Paragraph
fields.value: One or two for most teeth. Straightforward cases can be completed in a single longer visit; teeth with active infection often do better with a medicated dressing and a second appointment a week or two later.

fields.label: Text
fields.value: Do I really need a crown afterwards?

fields.label: Paragraph
fields.value: On back teeth, almost always. A root-treated molar without a crown has a significantly higher risk of splitting, and a split tooth usually has to come out - losing the tooth you just paid to save. Front teeth can sometimes be restored more conservatively.

fields.label: Text
fields.value: What if I just have it taken out instead?

fields.label: Paragraph
fields.value: That’s a legitimate choice, and cheaper today. Weigh it against the cost of replacing the tooth - an implant or bridge typically costs more than root canal treatment and a crown combined. We’ll give you both figures.

fields.label: Text
fields.value: Crowns & Bridges

fields.label: Text
fields.value: Crown or extraction - how do I decide?

fields.label: Paragraph
fields.value: It hinges on how much sound tooth and bone remain and whether the root is healthy. A tooth worth saving is usually worth saving, since replacing it costs more than crowning it. We’ll show you the X-ray and give you both paths with prices.

fields.label: Text
fields.value: How long do crowns last?

fields.label: Paragraph
fields.value: Ten to fifteen years is a fair expectation, and many last considerably longer. Grinding, decay at the margin and gum recession are what shorten them.

fields.label: Text
fields.value: Is a bridge better than an implant?

fields.label: Paragraph
fields.value: Neither is universally better. A bridge is faster and often cheaper, but requires cutting down two teeth. An implant preserves the neighbours and lasts longer, but costs more and takes months. If the adjacent teeth already need crowns, a bridge starts to make a lot of sense.

fields.label: Text
fields.value: What if my crown falls off?

fields.label: Paragraph
fields.value: Keep it, don’t attempt to glue it, and ring us. Often it can be re-cemented. In the meantime the exposed tooth will be sensitive and is weaker than it feels, so chew on the other side.

fields.label: Text
fields.value: Can I get a crown in one day?

fields.label: Paragraph
fields.value: For many cases, yes - our CEREC system scans, designs and mills the crown on site so it’s fitted at the same appointment. It isn’t suitable for every case, and we’ll tell you if yours needs a laboratory.

fields.label: Text
fields.value: Single-Visit Crowns (CEREC)

fields.label: Text
fields.value: Is a CEREC crown as good as a laboratory one?

fields.label: Paragraph
fields.value: For most cases, yes - the ceramic is strong, the fit is excellent and the digital scan is more accurate than putty. Where a lab still wins is complex front-tooth aesthetics and multi-unit bridges, and we’ll tell you when that applies to you.

fields.label: Text
fields.value: How long does the appointment take?

fields.label: Paragraph
fields.value: Usually around two hours from start to finish, including the milling time. You can bring something to read, watch the ceiling screen, or step out for a coffee while the crown mills.

fields.label: Text
fields.value: Does it hurt more than a normal crown?

fields.label: Paragraph
fields.value: No - it’s the same preparation under the same local anaesthetic. If anything it’s easier, because there’s no putty impression and no second round of numbing two weeks later.

fields.label: Text
fields.value: What if the crown doesn’t fit?

fields.label: Paragraph
fields.value: We check fit, contacts and bite before bonding anything, and because the design is on screen we can adjust and re-mill on the spot if needed. That’s a genuine advantage over sending work away.

fields.label: Text
fields.value: Dental Implants

fields.label: Text
fields.value: Does having an implant placed hurt?

fields.label: Paragraph
fields.value: Placement is done under local anaesthetic, and most people describe the appointment itself as easier than expected - comparable to having a tooth out. Afterwards you should expect swelling and soreness for a few days, managed with simple pain relief.

fields.label: Text
fields.value: How long do implants last?

fields.label: Paragraph
fields.value: Well-maintained implants can last decades, and the titanium post itself often lasts a lifetime. The crown on top is the part that wears - expect to replace it at some stage. Daily cleaning and regular check-ups matter more than anything else.

fields.label: Text
fields.value: Am I too old for an implant?

fields.label: Paragraph
fields.value: Age itself is rarely the barrier. Bone quality, general health, medications and smoking matter far more. We assess all of that before recommending anything.

fields.label: Text
fields.value: Can I have the tooth out and the implant in on the same day?

fields.label: Paragraph
fields.value: Sometimes - immediate placement is possible in the right conditions, with enough bone and no active infection. It isn’t suitable for every case and we won’t force it if the site isn’t right.

fields.label: Text
fields.value: What if I don’t have enough bone?

fields.label: Paragraph
fields.value: A bone graft can build the site up first, which adds time and cost. The 3D scan tells us early, so this comes up in planning rather than as a surprise on the day.

fields.label: Text
fields.value: Dentures

fields.label: Text
fields.value: How long does it take to get used to dentures?

fields.label: Paragraph
fields.value: Two to four weeks for most people to feel reasonably comfortable, and a few months to feel genuinely natural. Lower full dentures take longest. Persisting through the first fortnight is the hardest and most important part.

fields.label: Text
fields.value: Will people be able to tell?

fields.label: Paragraph
fields.value: Modern dentures are designed to look natural - slight irregularity, appropriate shade for your age, and proportions that suit your face. At the wax try-in you approve the appearance before anything is finalised, so bring someone whose eye you trust.

fields.label: Text
fields.value: Can I sleep in them?

fields.label: Paragraph
fields.value: Better not to. Leaving them out overnight lets the gum tissue recover and reduces the risk of fungal infection. Store them in water so the acrylic doesn’t dry out and distort.

fields.label: Text
fields.value: My denture has broken. Can you fix it?

fields.label: Paragraph
fields.value: Usually, yes. Bring all the pieces and don’t glue it - household adhesives contaminate the acrylic and can make a proper repair impossible. Many repairs are same-day.

fields.label: Text
fields.value: Why has my denture become loose?

fields.label: Paragraph
fields.value: Because the bone underneath continues to shrink after teeth are removed. It’s normal and not your fault. A reline refits the base to your current ridge and usually solves it; eventually a remake is needed.

fields.label: Text
fields.value: Orthodontics

fields.label: Text
fields.value: Am I too old for braces?

fields.label: Paragraph
fields.value: No. Teeth move at any age, provided the gums and bone are healthy - we treat plenty of adults. Treatment can take a little longer than in teenagers, and gum health is checked carefully first.

fields.label: Text
fields.value: Will I need to wear a retainer forever?

fields.label: Paragraph
fields.value: In some form, yes. Teeth have a lifelong tendency to drift back. Most people move to wearing a retainer at night only, indefinitely. It’s a small habit that protects a long investment.

fields.label: Text
fields.value: Metal Braces

fields.label: Text
fields.value: How long will I need braces?

fields.label: Paragraph
fields.value: Most courses run twelve to twenty-four months, with simple cases shorter and complex bites longer. We give you a range at the planning stage and revisit it as we go - broken brackets and missed appointments are what extend it.

fields.label: Text
fields.value: Do braces hurt?

fields.label: Paragraph
fields.value: Fitting them doesn’t. For a few days afterwards, and after each adjustment, teeth ache and biting feels tender - soft food and simple pain relief handle it. Cheeks and lips get irritated in the first week until they toughen up, which wax fixes.

fields.label: Text
fields.value: Are metal braces better than aligners?

fields.label: Paragraph
fields.value: For complex cases, often yes. They can achieve movements aligners struggle with, they work continuously without relying on you, and they cost less. Aligners win on appearance and convenience. It genuinely depends on the case, not on fashion.

fields.label: Text
fields.value: What happens if I don’t wear my retainer?

fields.label: Paragraph
fields.value: Your teeth drift back - reliably, and often within months. Retention is not optional, and the usual long-term routine is a retainer at night indefinitely. It’s a small habit that protects one or two years of work.

fields.label: Text
fields.value: Clear (Ceramic) Braces

fields.label: Text
fields.value: Are ceramic braces really less visible?

fields.label: Paragraph
fields.value: Considerably, yes - the brackets blend with tooth colour and from conversational distance they’re easy to miss. They’re not invisible: you’ll see them up close, and the wire is still there.

fields.label: Text
fields.value: Do the brackets stain?

fields.label: Paragraph
fields.value: The ceramic itself doesn’t. The elastic ties holding the wire do, especially with coffee, tea, red wine, curry and smoking. They’re replaced at each adjustment, so any staining is temporary - but it’s worth knowing before you choose them.

fields.label: Text
fields.value: Do they hurt more than metal braces?

fields.label: Paragraph
fields.value: No, the discomfort is comparable - a few days of aching after fitting and each adjustment. Ceramic brackets are slightly bulkier, so cheek irritation early on can be marginally more noticeable. Wax solves it.

fields.label: Text
fields.value: How long will I be in them?

fields.label: Paragraph
fields.value: Most cases run twelve to twenty-four months depending on complexity. Broken brackets and missed adjustments are what stretch that out, and both are largely within your control.

fields.label: Text
fields.value: Clear Aligners

fields.label: Text
fields.value: How long does treatment take?

fields.label: Paragraph
fields.value: Simple cases can finish in around six months; more involved cases run twelve to eighteen months or longer. Your digital plan gives an estimate at the start, and wear time is the main variable that changes it.

fields.label: Text
fields.value: Are aligners as effective as braces?

fields.label: Paragraph
fields.value: For crowding, spacing and mild to moderate corrections, yes. For complex rotations, large movements and significant bite changes, fixed braces remain more predictable. We’ll tell you honestly which category your case falls into rather than sell you the appliance you asked for.

fields.label: Text
fields.value: Can I eat with them in?

fields.label: Paragraph
fields.value: No - take them out for everything except water. Chewing with trays in damages them, and eating or drinking anything sugary with them in traps sugar against your enamel for hours.

fields.label: Text
fields.value: What if I lose one?

fields.label: Paragraph
fields.value: Ring us. Depending on where you are in the sequence we’ll have you go back to the previous tray or forward to the next, and order a replacement. Don’t simply leave them out - teeth start moving back within days.

fields.label: Text
fields.value: Is it Invisalign?

fields.label: Paragraph
fields.value: We provide clear aligner treatment. [VERIFY] whether the practice is a current Invisalign provider and licensed to use the brand name - until that’s confirmed we describe the treatment generically.

fields.label: Text
fields.value: How quickly can you see me?

fields.label: Paragraph
fields.value: Usually the same day. Call {{site:phone}} as early as you can and we’ll fit you into the emergency time we keep aside each day. Walk-ins are welcome too, though calling ahead means less waiting.

fields.label: Text
fields.value: Will the visit hurt?

fields.label: Paragraph
fields.value: Our first job is to make you comfortable - local anaesthetic before anything sensitive, an explanation before every step, and we go at your pace. Most people tell us the anticipation was worse than the visit.

fields.label: Text
fields.value: What will an emergency visit cost?

fields.label: Paragraph
fields.value: The visit starts with an examination and usually an X-ray so we can find the cause, and we quote any treatment before it starts. Health funds are claimable on the spot with HICAPS, and payment plans are available - see our fees and payment plans page.

fields.label: Text
fields.value: What should I do if it happens after hours?

fields.label: Paragraph
fields.value: Call {{site:phone}} and follow the recorded guidance, then book the first available appointment online. If you have facial swelling affecting breathing or swallowing, uncontrolled bleeding or a suspected broken jaw, call 000 or go to the nearest emergency department.
